nodes.text: 54. After this they came to Chromatius, saying to him: ‘When we broke the idols, you ought to have recovered your health, unless perhaps some signs of unbelief are left behind in your mind. For we hold this as certain among us: either there is something that has not yet been broken, or, if everything has been broken, show us more plainly what you are harbouring in your mind.’ Then he said: ‘I have a chamber made entirely of glass, in which the whole science of the stars and of astrology has been built by mechanical art; on its construction my father Tarquinius is known to have spent more than two hundred pounds of gold.’ Saint Sebastian said to him: ‘If you wish to keep this intact, you break yourself.’ Chromatius said: ‘Why so? Are astrology or the ephemerides worshipped with any use of sacrifices, when by them only the courses of months and years are marked off by a fixed number through the spaces of the hours, and the fullness or waning of the lunar globe is foreseen by the motion of the fingers, under the guidance of reason and by reckoning with counters?’ Saint Polycarp the presbyter said: ‘There are the signs of Leo and Capricorn and Sagittarius and Scorpio and Taurus; there the moon in Aries, the hour in Cancer; in Jupiter a star, in Mercury the tropic, in Venus Mars; and in all these monstrous demons an art hostile to God is recognised. Christians reject these things so thoroughly that not only do they themselves not have them, not worship them, not believe them, not keep them, but they do not even share the minds of those who fill their breasts with trifles of this kind. For all these things are false and servants of deception: there is a likeness of truth in them, not truth itself.’
